Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual PMIERs Section 802(5) reinsurance report to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac — consolidated non-lender-captive report plus the ten individual top-reinsurer reports; escalates ceded-credit questions to the Head of Reinsurance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PMIERs (Sept 27, 2018) Section 802(5) reinsurance reporting, re-read against the current Enterprise-published PMIERs text and any FHFA/Enterprise PMIERs amendment or Approved Insurer letter issued since the last annual submission

In-scope processes.value: Ceded reinsurance administration for the mortgage guaranty book — treaty and ILN inventory, lender-captive vs non-lender-captive classification, ceded risk-in-force calculation by counterparty, top-10 ranking, and the annual Enterprise reinsurance report pack

In-scope systems.value: Ceded treaty/ILN records, cession statements and ceded risk-in-force by counterparty; treaty documents and Enterprise no-objection letters in the treaty repository; report pack assembled in Microsoft Excel and transmitted through the Enterprise-designated secure MI reporting channel

Compliance procedure documented.value: PMIERs 802(5) Reinsurance Reporting Procedure — captive/non-captive classification test, ceded RIF calculation from the Exhibit F loan-level dataset, top-10 counterparty ranking by aggregate ceded RIF, per-reinsurer report template, Schedule F Part 3 reconciliation and dual-Enterprise transmission steps

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Financial Officer and the Head of Reinsurance; re-approved annually before the April cycle and on any PMIERs amendment or Enterprise reinsurance-approval condition change

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle on the December 31 as-of date, submitted to both Enterprises by April 15 of the following year; any new or amended non-lender-captive reinsurance agreement is reported within 30 calendar days of execution rather than waiting for the annual cycle

Deadline reminders configured.value: Regulatory reporting calendar tasks at Jan 31 (data cut), Feb 28 (ceded RIF and ranking complete), Mar 15 (draft pack to CFO), Mar 31 (sign-off) and Apr 8 (transmission) against the April 15 due date, with a 30-day clock opened automatically when a new cession is booked

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Submitted consolidated and top-10 reports, the ceded RIF extract, the Schedule F Part 3 reconciliation, Enterprise no-objection letters and both Enterprises' receipt confirmations retained 7 years from the as-of date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed April 15 submission, an omitted non-lender-captive counterparty, or ceded RIF that does not tie to the Exhibit F dataset is logged as a PMIERs reporting exception with root cause, owner, corrected-report date and Enterprise notification status

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CFO signs the annual submission certification and every corrected or late resubmission to the Enterprises

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every ceded reinsurance and insurance-linked note transaction in force at any point in the reporting year per the reinsurance administration system, plus every counterparty appearing in Schedule F Part 3 of the annual statutory statement

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on completeness — any non-lender-captive agreement absent from the consolidated report, or any of the top-10 reinsurers by aggregate ceded RIF missing an individual report, is a fail; ceded RIF per counterparty must tie to the Exhibit F loan-level dataset within 0.5%, and submission after April 15 is an automatic fail

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual (December 31 as-of, April 15 submission); the test runs once per year on the submitted pack, with an interim check each quarter that newly executed cessions were reported inside their 30-day window

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Auditor must not have prepared the ceded RIF extract, the counterparty ranking or any individual reinsurer report

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual PMIERs 802(5) reinsurance reporting workpaper — population extract, Schedule F reconciliation, sample selection, ceded RIF re-performance, ranking recalculation and exception log — filed in the compliance evidence repository under the reporting year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Consolidated non-lender-captive report, the ten individual reinsurer reports, executed treaty/ILN documents, Enterprise no-objection letters, collateral and trust statements and both transmission confirmations, producible to an Enterprise Approved Insurer review or an FHFA request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Reporting Manager answers Enterprise data queries through the Approved Insurer relationship contacts at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; the Head of Reinsurance owns ceded-credit and counterparty-concentration questions; General Counsel clears any disclosure of an unreported or non-approved cession before it is sent

checklist.step: Open the annual reporting cycle and freeze the December 31 as-of data cut
actions: Open a new PMIERs 802(5) cycle folder named <reporting year>-802-5 and record the as-of date December 31 and the April 15 submission date.

In the reinsurance administration system run the ceded treaty register for the year and set the extract as-of date to 31-Dec; ask the Reinsurance Ops Manager to confirm all fourth-quarter cession statements are booked and the period is closed.
List every quota share, excess-of-loss, aggregate excess and insurance-linked note transaction in force at any point in the year, including agreements that terminated or commuted mid-year.
Record for each: counterparty legal name, NAIC/FEIN or ILN issuer identifier, treaty reference, inception and expiry dates, cession percentage and attachment/detachment points.
Send the frozen register to the Ceded Reinsurance Analyst and the Reinsurance Accountant as the single source for the cycle.
checklist.done: a frozen December 31 ceded register exists in the cycle folder with all in-force and terminated agreements listed and confirmed closed by Reinsurance Operations.

checklist.step: Classify every agreement as lender-captive or non-lender-captive
actions: Open each executed agreement in the treaty repository and read the counterparty ownership clause and the parties' recitals.

Tag the agreement LENDER-CAPTIVE where the reinsurer is owned or controlled by, or affiliated with, an originating lender that also delivers loans insured by the company; otherwise tag NON-LENDER-CAPTIVE.

For any counterparty whose ownership is unclear, ask the Reinsurance Credit & Security Analyst for the current corporate ownership chart and the parent's ultimate controlling person and file it against the row.
Record on each row the classification, the clause or ownership document relied on, the page reference and the person deciding, with the date.
Hand the classification list to the Regulatory Reporting Manager — only NON-LENDER-CAPTIVE rows go into the consolidated report required by Section 802(5).
checklist.done: every agreement carries a captive/non-captive tag traced to a named clause or ownership document, with a decider and date.

checklist.step: Compute ceded risk-in-force by counterparty from the loan-level portfolio dataset
actions: Pull the December 31 Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset from the warehouse — the same certified extract delivered to the Enterprises — keyed on loan identifier, original and current UPB, coverage percentage and delinquency status.
Compute gross risk-in-force per loan as current UPB multiplied by the coverage percentage stated on the certificate.

Apply each treaty's cession terms to the loans in its covered cohort (policy vintage year band, book year, or delivery-lender group as the treaty defines it) to derive ceded RIF per loan per counterparty.

Sum ceded RIF to counterparty level and to aggregate level, and reconcile the total to the ceded RIF reported in the statutory annual statement Schedule F Part 3 with the Reinsurance Accountant; investigate any variance above 0.5%.
Save the counterparty ceded RIF schedule into the cycle folder with the query, the extract date and the row count.
checklist.done: ceded risk-in-force is calculated per counterparty from the Exhibit F dataset and ties to Schedule F Part 3 within 0.5%, with variances explained in writing.

checklist.step: Rank counterparties and fix the top-10 list by aggregate ceded risk-in-force
actions: Aggregate ceded RIF to ultimate parent group level so two subsidiaries of the same reinsurer are not ranked as separate counterparties.
Sort descending on aggregate ceded RIF and cut the top ten; record each counterparty's ceded RIF amount and its share of total ceded RIF and of total gross RIF.
Where a tie or a near-tie inside 1% sits on the tenth position, include both counterparties rather than choosing between them, and note why.
Show the change in rank and amount versus the prior year's submission so movement in concentration is visible to the reader.
Have the Head of Reinsurance initial the ranking before individual reports are drafted.
checklist.done: a ranked counterparty schedule exists, grouped to ultimate parent, with the top ten fixed and initialled by the Head of Reinsurance.

checklist.step: Collect counterparty credit, collateral and Enterprise-approval facts for each top-10 reinsurer
actions: For each top-10 counterparty record the current financial strength ratings from A.M. Best, S&P and Moody's with the rating date and any outlook change during the year.
Pull the collateral position: trust account balance, letters of credit with issuing bank and expiry, funds-withheld balance, and the December 31 statement from the trustee.
Retrieve the Enterprise no-objection or approval letter for the agreement from Fannie Mae and from Freddie Mac, with the letter date and any conditions attached to the ceded credit.
Note whether the counterparty is an authorised, accredited or certified reinsurer in the state of domicile, and any downgrade trigger or collateral step-up clause in the treaty.
File the rating sheets, trust statements and approval letters into the cycle folder under the counterparty name.
checklist.done: each top-10 counterparty has ratings, collateral balances, trustee statements and both Enterprises' approval letters on file.

checklist.step: Draft the consolidated non-lender-captive reinsurance report
actions: Build the consolidated schedule with one row per non-lender-captive agreement: counterparty and ultimate parent, agreement type (quota share, XOL, ILN), effective and expiry dates, covered book years, cession percentage, ceded RIF at December 31, ceded premium for the year and PMIERs credit taken.
Add total rows for ceded RIF, ceded premium and the PMIERs Minimum Required Asset relief claimed, and state ceded RIF as a percentage of total gross RIF.
Insert a narrative section describing counterparty concentration: top-1, top-5 and top-10 shares of ceded RIF and the year-over-year movement.
State the as-of date, the preparer, the data source (Exhibit F December 31 dataset) and the Schedule F Part 3 reconciliation result on the cover page.
Circulate the draft to the Head of Reinsurance and the Reinsurance Accountant for figure-by-figure confirmation.
checklist.done: the consolidated report covers every non-lender-captive agreement with ceded RIF, premium, PMIERs credit and concentration narrative, confirmed by Reinsurance.

checklist.step: Draft the ten individual top-reinsurer reports
actions: Produce one report per top-10 counterparty using the standard template: counterparty identity and domicile, group structure, agreements in force with the company, ceded RIF and ceded premium, collateral held, ratings and Enterprise approval references.
Show the counterparty's ceded RIF split by book year and by delinquency status so the Enterprise can see the quality of the ceded exposure.
State the aggregate exposure the company retains to that counterparty across all treaties, including any recoverable balance outstanding at December 31.
Attach the executed agreement and the current trust or letter-of-credit statement as exhibits to each report.
Name the file <counterparty>-802-5-<reporting year>.pdf and store it in the cycle folder.
checklist.done: ten individual reports exist, each with exposure, collateral, ratings, approvals and the executed agreement attached.

checklist.step: Reconcile the report pack to the statutory statement and the general ledger
actions: Tie total ceded premium in the pack to the ceded premium accounts in the general ledger for the year and to the annual statement Underwriting and Investment Exhibit.
Tie ceded RIF and recoverable balances to Schedule F Part 3 line by line, listing any counterparty appearing in one source but not the other.
Confirm the contingency reserve and unearned premium ceded amounts used in the PMIERs credit calculation agree with the filed statutory blank.
Document each reconciling item with an amount, a cause and a sign-off, and clear anything that indicates a booking error before the pack moves on.
Sign the reconciliation sheet and file it in the cycle folder.
checklist.done: a signed reconciliation ties the pack to the general ledger and Schedule F Part 3 with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Review the ceded-credit treatment against the PMIERs reinsurance conditions
actions: For each agreement claiming PMIERs Minimum Required Asset relief, read the Enterprise approval letter and confirm the relief taken matches the approved structure and any cap or condition it carries.
Confirm no relief is claimed on an agreement that has not received both Enterprises' non-objection, and flag any structure amended since approval.
Check downgrade and collateral triggers were not breached during the year; where a trigger fired, confirm the collateral step-up was actually made and dated.
Record a written conclusion per agreement that the ceded credit claimed remains supportable, and list any agreement whose credit must be withdrawn.
checklist.done: every claimed PMIERs credit is matched to an unconditioned Enterprise approval, or is withdrawn with the reason recorded.

checklist.step: Obtain legal review of counterparty disclosure and confidentiality terms
actions: Read each top-10 agreement's confidentiality clause and confirm disclosure to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac under PMIERs Section 802(5) is permitted or falls within the regulatory-disclosure carve-out.
Where a clause requires notice to the counterparty before disclosure, issue that notice and file the sent copy with the date.
Confirm the executed agreements attached as exhibits are the final signed versions, including all amendments and side letters.
Clear the pack for transmission in writing, noting any redaction agreed with the counterparty and the basis for it.
checklist.done: counsel has cleared the pack for transmission with any counterparty notices issued and redactions justified.

checklist.step: Obtain CFO certification of the submission
actions: Review the consolidated report, the ten individual reports and the signed Schedule F reconciliation together in one sitting.
Challenge the concentration narrative: ask what happens to Available Assets and the PMIERs sufficiency ratio if the largest counterparty's credit is disallowed.
Sign the certification page stating the reports are complete and accurate as of December 31 and prepared under PMIERs Section 802(5).
Route the signed certification through DocuSign and store the completed envelope in the cycle folder.
checklist.done: a dated CFO certification covering completeness and accuracy is executed and filed with the pack.

checklist.step: Transmit the pack to Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac by April 15
actions: Submit the consolidated report, the ten individual reports and the CFO certification through each Enterprise's designated secure MI reporting channel — Fannie Mae's Approved Insurer submission site and Freddie Mac's secure file transfer for MI reporting — no later than April 15.
Copy the Approved Insurer relationship contact at each Enterprise on the transmittal email, stating the reporting period, the as-of date and the PMIERs section being satisfied.
Capture the upload confirmation, the transmission timestamp and the file manifest from each channel as separate PDFs.
If either channel rejects a file for size or format, resubmit the same business day and record both attempts — never let a rejection sit past the deadline.
Update the regulatory reporting calendar entry to Submitted with the two confirmation references.
checklist.done: both Enterprises hold the full pack, with dated upload confirmations captured on or before April 15.

checklist.step: Report new or amended cessions inside the 30-day window
actions: When a new non-lender-captive agreement, amendment, commutation or ILN is executed, open a 30-calendar-day reporting clock from the execution date in the regulatory reporting calendar.
Prepare the interim notice: counterparty, structure, covered cohort, ceded RIF at inception, PMIERs credit sought and the Enterprise approval reference.
Send the notice to both Enterprises' Approved Insurer contacts before the clock expires and file the confirmation.
Add the agreement to the current-year ceded register so it carries into the next April 15 consolidated report automatically.
checklist.done: every mid-year cession has a dated Enterprise notice inside 30 days of execution and is on the register for the annual report.

checklist.step: Handle Enterprise follow-up questions and issue corrections
actions: Log every Enterprise question on the submission as a tracker item with the date received, the Enterprise, the question text and the response due date.
Draft the answer with the Head of Reinsurance, referencing the underlying treaty clause or ceded RIF query, and have counsel clear anything touching a counterparty's confidential terms.
Where an error is found, reissue the affected report marked 'Corrected — supersedes <date>' with a change summary and a fresh CFO certification.
Record the resolution and the Enterprise acknowledgement on the tracker item and close it.
checklist.done: every Enterprise query and every correction is tracked to a dated, acknowledged resolution.

checklist.step: Archive the cycle evidence under the retention label
actions: Move the cycle folder — ceded register, classification list, ceded RIF schedule, ranking, ten reports, consolidated report, reconciliation, approval letters, CFO certification and both upload confirmations — into the compliance evidence repository under PMIERs / 802(5) / <reporting year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the December 31 as-of date.
Confirm the record is indexed and retrievable by counterparty name, reporting year and agreement reference.
Record the archive location on the regulatory reporting calendar entry so the next cycle starts from it.
checklist.done: the full cycle record is archived, labelled for 7-year retention and searchable by counterparty and year.

testing.step: Build the independent population of ceded agreements for the year
actions: Extract from the reinsurance administration system every ceded agreement and ILN with any period of coverage inside the reporting year, independent of the reporting team's register.
Add agreements booked after the December 31 close but with an inception date in the year, and agreements commuted or terminated mid-year.
Cross-check the extract against the contract lifecycle management repository for executed reinsurance contracts signed during the year.
Sign the population as complete, recording the extract query, date and row count in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently extracted, signed population of ceded agreements exists and includes mid-year terminations and late-booked cessions.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to Schedule F Part 3 and to the submitted consolidated report
actions: Match every population counterparty to a Schedule F Part 3 line in the filed annual statement and to a row in the submitted consolidated report.
List every counterparty present in one source and absent from another, and obtain a written explanation from the Reinsurance Accountant for each.
Confirm any counterparty excluded from the consolidated report is excluded solely because it is tagged lender-captive, and that the tag has a clause reference.
Treat an unexplained omission from the submitted report as an automatic exception with no materiality threshold.
testing.done: every population counterparty is reconciled to Schedule F Part 3 and to the report, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of agreements
actions: Take 100% of the ten counterparties reported individually plus every agreement tagged lender-captive.
Take 15 further agreements selected at random with a recorded seed from the remaining non-lender-captive population.
Record the seed, the population size, the selection date and the resulting agreement list so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Add any agreement carrying a prior-year exception as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample is drawn covering all top-10 and all captive-tagged agreements plus a seeded random selection.

testing.step: Re-perform the lender-captive classification on the sample
actions: Open each sampled executed agreement in the treaty repository and read the parties, recitals and ownership clauses before looking at the recorded tag.
Reach your own captive / non-captive conclusion and record the clause and page you relied on.
Compare to the recorded classification; a non-captive agreement wrongly tagged captive — and therefore left out of the consolidated report — is a reportable breach, not a documentation gap.
Where ownership turns on a corporate chart, verify the chart date is within the reporting year.
testing.done: each sampled agreement has an independent classification conclusion with a cited clause, and differences are logged.

testing.step: Recompute ceded risk-in-force from the Exhibit F dataset for sampled counterparties
actions: Pull the December 31 Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset as delivered to the Enterprises and recompute gross RIF per loan as current UPB times coverage percentage.
Apply the sampled treaty's covered cohort definition and cession percentage independently and total ceded RIF for that counterparty.
Compare to the reported figure; anything outside the 0.5% tolerance is an exception and must be traced to a specific cohort or coverage-field difference.
Confirm the dataset used for the report is the same certified extract delivered to the Enterprises, by comparing row counts and control totals.
testing.done: ceded RIF for every sampled counterparty is independently recomputed and agrees within 0.5%, or the difference is explained and logged.

testing.step: Recalculate the top-10 ranking and the parent-group aggregation
actions: Re-aggregate ceded RIF to ultimate parent group using the ownership charts on file and re-sort descending.
Compare your top ten to the reported top ten; a counterparty displaced by an aggregation error is an exception even if the totals are correct.
Recompute the top-1, top-5 and top-10 concentration percentages quoted in the narrative.
Check the boundary: confirm the eleventh counterparty's ceded RIF is genuinely below the tenth and that near-ties were disclosed.
testing.done: the reported top-10 list and concentration percentages are independently reproduced, with any displacement logged.

testing.step: Trace Enterprise approvals, collateral and ratings for each top-10 counterparty
actions: For each top-10 counterparty, open the Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac no-objection letters and confirm both exist, pre-date the credit taken, and cover the structure as currently amended.
Agree the collateral figures in the report to the December 31 trustee statement, letter-of-credit face amount and funds-withheld ledger balance.
Confirm the ratings quoted match the rating agency's published rating at December 31, not a stale prior-year rating.
Where a downgrade trigger fired during the year, confirm the collateral step-up was executed and dated inside the treaty's cure period.
testing.done: each top-10 counterparty's approvals, collateral balances and ratings are traced to primary documents dated at or before December 31.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline compliance for the annual and interim submissions
actions: Read the upload confirmation timestamps from both Enterprise channels and compare each to the April 15 due date.
For every agreement executed during the year, compute execution date plus 30 calendar days and compare it to the dated interim notice confirmation.
List every submission made after its date, with the number of days late and whether the Enterprise was told.
Confirm any resubmission following a channel rejection carries a same-business-day timestamp.
testing.done: annual and 30-day interim submission dates are recomputed and every late submission is quantified in days.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with the counterparty, the agreement reference, the defect and the effect on reported ceded RIF or PMIERs credit.
Assign a root cause — misclassified captive, wrong cohort mapping, stale ownership chart, missed 30-day clock, late transmission — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the reported figures were wrong, require a corrected report to the Enterprises with a fresh CFO certification.
Carry every open exception into next year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a corrected-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-omission and 0.5% ceded RIF tolerances and state whether each threshold was met.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — with the workpaper references supporting it.
Have the reviewer, who prepared none of the reports or extracts, sign the workpaper and confirm segregation in writing.
Report the conclusion and any Enterprise-reportable defect to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with an exception rate, a stated conclusion and an Audit Committee reporting date is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the PMIERs Available Assets / Minimum Required Assets self-assessment under the 2024 amended Available Asset standard, including the 24-month phase-in to full effect on September 30, 2026, and presents it to the Board Risk Committee

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FHFA/Enterprises PMIERs 2024 amendment on the Available Asset standard (24-month phase-in, fully effective 9/30/2026) read alongside PMIERs (Sept 27, 2018) Exhibit A availability-of-assets categories and Section 402 property valuation; re-verified each quarter against the Enterprises' published amendment and any Approved Insurer implementation letter

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly PMIERs sufficiency assessment — investment holdings classification into amended Exhibit A asset categories, residential-mortgage-backed and commercial-real-estate concentration limits, phase-in factor application, Minimum Required Asset calculation from the Exhibit F loan-level dataset, cushion forecasting and Board Risk Committee attestation

In-scope systems.value: Investment holdings, NAIC designations, credit ratings and liquidity classifications from the portfolio system; MRA computed off the Exhibit F loan-level dataset in the enterprise data warehouse; the self-assessment pack and board attestation held on the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: PMIERs Available Assets Self-Assessment Procedure — Exhibit A category mapping by credit quality and liquidity, RMBS/CRE-backed asset limits, phase-in factor table by quarter through 9/30/2026, MRA factor application, sufficiency ratio and cushion calculation, ALCO remediation triggers and board attestation route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Risk Officer and the Chief Investment Officer, ratified by the Board Risk Committee; re-approved each time the Enterprises publish a phase-in step or amend Exhibit A

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Quarterly assessment and Approved Insurer certification submitted within 45 calendar days of each quarter-end; the annual assessment with audited financial support submitted by April 15; any event that puts Available Assets below Minimum Required Assets is notified to both Enterprises within 30 calendar days; full Available Asset standard effective September 30, 2026

Deadline reminders configured.value: Capital calendar tasks at quarter-end +10 business days (holdings classified), +25 days (draft pack), +35 days (CRO attestation and board circulation) against the 45-day certification date, plus a standing April 15 annual task and an automatic 30-day clock opened by any sufficiency breach flag

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Quarterly Available Assets classification file, MRA calculation, phase-in workings, sufficiency ratio pack, model validation memo, CRO attestation and Board Risk Committee minutes retained 7 years from the quarter-end date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A misclassified Exhibit A asset, a breach of the RMBS/CRE concentration limit, an incorrectly applied phase-in factor, or a sufficiency ratio below 100% is logged as a capital-compliance exception with root cause, remediation plan, Enterprise notification date and cure deadline

Remediation sign-off captured.value: CRO signs the quarterly self-assessment attestation and every remediation plan arising from a classification error or sufficiency shortfall before it goes to the Board Risk Committee

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every investment holding in the Approved Insurer's portfolio at the quarter-end valuation date claimed as an Available Asset, plus the loan-level records in that quarter's Exhibit F dataset driving the Minimum Required Asset calculation

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Available Assets must equal or exceed Minimum Required Assets at every quarter-end — a sufficiency ratio below 100% is an immediate fail and a 30-day Enterprise notification; a cushion below the board-set 115% floor is a management-action trigger; any asset classified into a more favourable Exhibit A category than the amended standard permits, or any RMBS/CRE holding above its limit, is a fail regardless of the ratio

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is assessed quarterly with an annual board-approved self-assessment; the test runs each quarter on that quarter's holdings and MRA, with an expanded annual test covering the phase-in factor schedule through September 30, 2026

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be outside Capital Management and Investments and must not have classified any sampled holding or run the MRA calculation

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly PMIERs sufficiency test workpaper — holdings population, classification re-performance, concentration limit recalculation, phase-in factor check, MRA recomputation and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository under the quarter-end date

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Available Assets classification schedule with Exhibit A category and source rating per holding, MRA calculation with Exhibit F reconciliation, phase-in workings, sufficiency ratio history, CRO attestation and board minutes, producible to an Enterprise Approved Insurer review or FHFA request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Capital Management fronts Enterprise questions on Available Assets and MRA through the Approved Insurer contacts at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; the CFO owns any sufficiency shortfall notification and remediation commitment; General Counsel clears any statement about a projected breach before it is sent

checklist.step: Open the quarterly assessment and set the phase-in step in force
actions: Open a quarter folder named PMIERs-AA-<yyyy>Q<n> and record the valuation date, the 45-calendar-day certification due date and, for Q4, the April 15 annual date.
Read the Enterprises' published phase-in schedule for the 2024 Available Asset amendment and record which step applies at this quarter-end on the way to full effect on September 30, 2026.
Write the applicable haircut and eligibility factors for the quarter onto the phase-in control sheet, citing the amendment paragraph for each.
Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Manager that no Approved Insurer letter has changed the step since last quarter, and file the confirmation.
checklist.done: the quarter folder states the valuation date, the certification due date and the exact phase-in step with cited factors.

checklist.step: Extract the quarter-end investment holdings and their credit and liquidity attributes
actions: Run the holdings report in Aladdin as of the quarter-end valuation date at CUSIP level with book value, fair value, accrued interest, issuer, sector and maturity.
Attach to each holding its NAIC designation, agency credit ratings with rating dates, and a liquidity marker (daily-traded government, investment-grade corporate, private placement, structured).

Flag every position backed by residential mortgages (agency and non-agency RMBS, CMOs) or commercial real estate (CMBS, mortgage loans, real estate equity) as those drive the amended standard's limits.
Reconcile total book value to the general ledger investment accounts with the Controller and resolve differences before releasing the file.
Deliver the reconciled holdings file to Capital Management with the run timestamp and position count.
checklist.done: a GL-reconciled quarter-end holdings file exists with ratings, liquidity markers and RMBS/CRE flags on every position.

checklist.step: Classify each holding into the amended Exhibit A availability category
actions: Map each holding to its Exhibit A category using the amended standard's credit-quality and liquidity differentiation — cash and Treasuries, agency debt, investment-grade corporates by NAIC designation band, below-investment-grade, and mortgage-backed categories.
Apply the category's availability percentage or haircut for the phase-in step in force this quarter and compute the recognised Available Asset amount per holding.

Exclude outright anything the standard does not permit as an Available Asset — affiliate investments, non-admitted assets, encumbered or pledged securities, and assets held in a captive or funds-withheld arrangement.
Record on each row the category, the factor applied, the amendment paragraph relied on and the classifier's name and date.
Send the classified file to the ALM / Asset-Liability Actuary for a second read on every structured and private-placement position.
checklist.done: every holding carries an Exhibit A category, an applied factor with a cited paragraph, and a named classifier.

checklist.step: Apply the residential-mortgage and commercial-real-estate concentration limits
actions: Total the recognised value of assets backed by residential mortgages and, separately, by commercial real estate, and express each as a percentage of total Available Assets before limits.
Compare each percentage to the amendment's limit for the phase-in step in force and compute the excess that must be disallowed.
Disallow the excess starting with the lowest-credit-quality, least-liquid positions inside the breached bucket, and show the disallowance line by line.

Explain in the working paper why these limits exist — value loss on mortgage-backed assets during a housing stress correlates with the very claims PMIERs capital must cover — and state the post-limit recognised total.
Alert the Chief Investment Officer where a limit is breached so reinvestment can move the portfolio before next quarter-end.
checklist.done: RMBS and CRE-backed concentrations are measured against the standard's limits with any excess disallowed position by position.

checklist.step: Compute the Minimum Required Assets from the loan-level portfolio dataset
actions: Load the quarter's Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset — the same certified extract delivered to the Enterprises — and confirm the row count and RIF control total match the delivered file.

Apply the PMIERs Exhibit B risk-based required asset factors to net risk-in-force by loan attribute segment: original LTV band, credit score band, vintage, performing versus delinquent status and delinquency bucket.
Apply the applicable multipliers and any floor per loan, then subtract approved ceded-reinsurance and ILN relief only to the extent both Enterprises' no-objection letters permit.
Confirm with the Regulatory Reporting Analyst that the ceded relief taken agrees with the PMIERs credit shown in the reinsurance reporting pack.
Total the Minimum Required Assets and store the calculation with its input hash, run date and model version.
checklist.done: MRA is computed from the certified Exhibit F dataset with Exhibit B factors and reconciled ceded relief, with a versioned, reproducible run.

checklist.step: Calculate the sufficiency ratio and the capital cushion
actions: Compute the sufficiency ratio as post-limit Available Assets divided by Minimum Required Assets and the absolute cushion in dollars.
Compare the ratio to the PMIERs 100% floor and to the board-set operating cushion floor, and state the headroom in both percentage and dollar terms.
Show the walk from last quarter: new insurance written, delinquency migration, cures and claims paid, portfolio value changes, phase-in step change, and any ceded credit movement.
Isolate how much of the quarter's movement is caused purely by the amended Available Asset standard's tightening, so management can see the run-rate to September 30, 2026.
Flag immediately to the CFO and CRO if the ratio is below the operating floor or projected to fall below it within four quarters.
checklist.done: the sufficiency ratio, cushion and a quarter-on-quarter attribution walk are computed, with the phase-in impact isolated.

checklist.step: Project the sufficiency ratio through full effectiveness on September 30, 2026
actions: Roll the current portfolio and holdings forward quarter by quarter to September 30, 2026 applying each published phase-in step in turn.
Layer in planned new insurance written volumes from the business plan and the expected delinquency path from the reserving actuary.
Produce the projected sufficiency ratio for every quarter to 9/30/2026 and identify the first quarter, if any, where it falls below the operating floor.
Quantify the incremental Available Assets needed at that quarter and hand the number to Treasury and the Chief Investment Officer as the reinvestment or capital-raise target.
Document the assumptions, the model version and the run date in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: a quarter-by-quarter projection to 9/30/2026 exists with the first shortfall quarter and the dollar gap named.

checklist.step: Validate the classification logic and the MRA model independently
actions: Re-derive the Exhibit A category for a benchmark set of 30 holdings spanning every category using the amendment text alone, and compare to the production mapping.
Re-run the MRA calculation on a held-out slice of the Exhibit F dataset with an independently coded factor lookup and compare totals.
Test the boundary rules: a bond one notch either side of a category break, a position pledged part-way through the quarter, and a loan moving between delinquency buckets at the valuation date.
Write a validation memo with findings, severity and required fixes, and log it against the model record with the model version tested.
checklist.done: a dated validation memo covering category mapping, MRA recomputation and boundary cases is filed against the model version.

checklist.step: Assemble the self-assessment report pack
actions: Build the pack: sufficiency ratio and cushion, Available Assets by Exhibit A category, RMBS/CRE concentration positions against limits, MRA by loan segment, the attribution walk, the projection to 9/30/2026 and the validation memo findings.
Add the risk narrative — housing-stress sensitivity of the mortgage-backed holdings, delinquency migration risk, and counterparty dependence on ceded credit.
State each management action being taken: reinvestment away from limited asset classes, contingent capital arrangements, or a reduction in new insurance written.
Circulate the draft to the CFO, CRO and Chief Investment Officer for comment at least five business days before the board paper deadline.
checklist.done: a complete self-assessment pack with ratio, limits, projection, validation findings and named management actions is circulated for executive comment.

checklist.step: Take the sufficiency result and remediation plan through ALCO
actions: Table the concentration positions and disallowances at the Asset-Liability Committee with the reinvestment options that restore recognised Available Assets.
Decide and minute the portfolio actions: which mortgage-backed positions to reduce, which eligible categories to buy into, and the timetable relative to the next quarter-end.

Where the projection shows a shortfall before 9/30/2026, ask Treasury for the funding options — holding company downstream, contingent capital facility, or ceded reinsurance — with cost and lead time.
Record each action with an owner and a completion date and hand the minute to the Enterprise Risk Manager for the board pack.
checklist.done: ALCO has minuted portfolio and funding actions with owners and dates that close the projected gap.

checklist.step: Obtain the CRO attestation on the self-assessment
actions: Review the sufficiency ratio, the Exhibit A classification approach, the concentration disallowances and the validation memo findings together.
Challenge the two positions that most improve the ratio and ask the classifier to justify each against the amendment text.
Sign the attestation that Available Assets are recognised in line with the amended standard at the phase-in step in force and that the assessment is complete and accurate at the valuation date.
Record any qualification in the attestation itself rather than in a side note, and name the remediation owner for it.
checklist.done: a dated CRO attestation, including any qualification and its owner, is signed and attached to the pack.

checklist.step: Present the self-assessment to the Board Risk Committee and record the sign-off
actions: Publish the pack to the board portal at least five business days before the Risk Committee meeting with the CRO attestation attached.
Present the sufficiency ratio, the cushion against the PMIERs 100% floor, the projection to September 30, 2026 and the ALCO actions.
Capture in the minutes the committee's resolution approving the self-assessment, any additional action it directs, and the directors present.
Have the Corporate Secretary finalise the minute extract and file it with the quarter folder as the evidence of board sign-off.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has resolved on the self-assessment and a signed minute extract is filed with the quarter pack.

checklist.step: Certify and submit to the Enterprises within 45 calendar days of quarter-end
actions: Prepare the Approved Insurer quarterly certification showing Available Assets, Minimum Required Assets and the sufficiency ratio at the valuation date, signed by the CEO and CFO.

Submit the certification with the supporting Available Assets classification schedule to Fannie Mae's Approved Insurer submission site and Freddie Mac's secure MI file transfer no later than quarter-end plus 45 calendar days; use April 15 for the annual submission with the audited financial support.
Capture both upload confirmations with timestamps and file them in the quarter folder.
Update the capital calendar entry to Submitted and record the two confirmation references.
checklist.done: both Enterprises hold the certification and classification schedule, with confirmations dated inside the 45-day window (April 15 for the annual).

checklist.step: Notify the Enterprises within 30 calendar days of a shortfall or material change
actions: Where Available Assets fall below Minimum Required Assets, or a material change in asset eligibility or ceded credit is identified, open a 30-calendar-day notification clock from the date the condition is identified.
Draft the notice stating the shortfall amount, the cause, the remediation plan with dates, and the expected quarter of cure; have General Counsel clear it before sending.
Send it to the Approved Insurer contacts at both Enterprises inside the 30 days and log the acknowledgement.
Report the notice and the Enterprise response to the Board Risk Committee at its next sitting.
checklist.done: any shortfall or material eligibility change is notified to both Enterprises inside 30 calendar days with a dated remediation plan.

checklist.step: Archive the quarter's assessment evidence
actions: Move the quarter folder — holdings file, classification schedule with factors and citations, concentration workings, MRA run, projection, validation memo, ALCO minute, CRO attestation, board minute extract and submission confirmations — into the compliance evidence repository under PMIERs / Available Assets / <quarter>.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the quarter-end valuation date.
Confirm the record is retrievable by quarter-end date, sufficiency ratio and phase-in step.
Carry the phase-in control sheet forward as the opening input for the next quarter.
checklist.done: the quarter's full assessment record is archived, labelled for 7-year retention and searchable by quarter and phase-in step.

testing.step: Build the population of holdings claimed as Available Assets
actions: Extract the full quarter-end holdings list from Aladdin independently of the Capital Management file, at CUSIP level with book value, fair value, issuer and NAIC designation.
Add pledged, encumbered and funds-withheld positions and affiliate investments so exclusions can be tested rather than assumed.
Reconcile the extract's total book value to the general ledger investment accounts and to the statutory Schedule D total, resolving differences before sampling.
Sign the population as complete with the extract query, timestamp and position count in the workpaper.
testing.done: an independently extracted holdings population is reconciled to the general ledger and Schedule D and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the submitted Available Assets classification schedule
actions: Match every population position to a row on the classification schedule submitted with the Approved Insurer certification.
List positions on the schedule with no population match and population positions absent from the schedule, and obtain a written explanation for each.
Confirm every excluded position is excluded for a stated reason permitted by the amended standard — pledged, affiliate, non-admitted, funds-withheld — and not simply dropped.
Tie the schedule's recognised Available Assets total to the figure in the certification sent to both Enterprises.
testing.done: the holdings population, the classification schedule and the certified Available Assets total reconcile line for line.

testing.step: Draw a documented, risk-weighted sample of holdings
actions: Take 100% of positions flagged as residential-mortgage or commercial-real-estate backed and 100% of positions above the individual materiality threshold set at 1% of Available Assets.
Take 30 further positions at random with a recorded seed, stratified across Exhibit A categories so every category is represented.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
Add every holding that carried a classification exception last quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering all mortgage-backed and material positions plus a stratified random selection is drawn.

testing.step: Re-perform the Exhibit A classification against the amended standard
actions: For each sampled holding, read the security's terms, NAIC designation and rating as at the valuation date and derive the Exhibit A category from the 2024 amendment text before looking at the recorded category.
Apply the phase-in factor for the quarter from the Enterprises' published schedule and compute your own recognised amount.
Compare to the recorded classification and amount; a position placed in a more favourable credit-quality or liquidity category than the amendment allows is a fail, not a presentation difference.
Capture the amendment paragraph and the rating evidence relied on into the workpaper for each sampled position.
testing.done: each sampled holding has an independent category, factor and recognised amount with the source paragraph captured.

testing.step: Recalculate the residential-mortgage and commercial-real-estate concentration limits
actions: Re-total recognised RMBS-backed and CRE-backed values from the population and express each as a percentage of pre-limit Available Assets.
Compare to the limit applicable at this phase-in step and recompute the required disallowance independently.
Check the disallowance was applied to the lowest-quality, least-liquid positions in the breached bucket as the procedure requires, not to whichever positions minimise the impact.
Confirm no position was reclassified out of the mortgage-backed flag during the quarter without a documented reason.
testing.done: concentration percentages and disallowances are independently recomputed and agree, or the difference is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the Minimum Required Assets from the certified loan-level dataset
actions: Pull the quarter's Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset as delivered to the Enterprises and verify the row count and RIF control total against the delivery manifest.
Apply the Exhibit B factors independently by LTV band, credit score band, vintage and delinquency bucket, using a separately coded lookup rather than the production model.
Compare the independent MRA total to the reported figure and explain any variance above 0.25% down to a named segment.
Confirm ceded relief subtracted is limited to structures covered by both Enterprises' no-objection letters, by tracing to the letters themselves.
testing.done: MRA is independently recomputed within 0.25%, with ceded relief traced to Enterprise approval letters.

testing.step: Verify the phase-in step applied against the published schedule
actions: Open the Enterprises' published 2024 Available Asset amendment phase-in schedule and identify the step in force at this quarter-end on the path to full effect on September 30, 2026.
Compare the factors on the phase-in control sheet to the published schedule factor by factor.
Confirm no factor was carried over from the prior quarter where the schedule moved, and that the schedule version used is the latest Enterprise publication.
Recompute the projected first-shortfall quarter using the correct schedule and compare it to the projection presented to the board.
testing.done: the applied phase-in factors match the published schedule and the projection to 9/30/2026 is reproduced.

testing.step: Trace the governance evidence and the submission dates
actions: Confirm a signed CRO attestation exists for the quarter and pre-dates the certification submission.
Open the Board Risk Committee minute on the board portal and confirm it records approval of the self-assessment, the directors present and any directed action.
Compute quarter-end plus 45 calendar days and compare it to the Enterprise upload confirmation timestamps; for the annual cycle compare to April 15.
Where a shortfall or material change occurred, compute identification date plus 30 calendar days and confirm the Enterprise notice was sent inside it.
testing.done: attestation, board approval and every 45-day, April 15 and 30-day date are traced to dated evidence.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the CUSIP or loan segment, the defect and the dollar effect on Available Assets, MRA or the sufficiency ratio.
Assign a root cause — stale rating, wrong Exhibit A category, missed phase-in step, unflagged mortgage-backed position, unapproved ceded relief — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the certified ratio was overstated, require a corrected certification to both Enterprises and assess whether the 30-day notification clock has started.
Carry every open exception into next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a quantified effect, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a re-certification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State whether the sufficiency ratio was at or above 100% at the valuation date and whether the board cushion floor was met, with the recomputed figures.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — referencing the classification, concentration, MRA and phase-in test results.
Have the independent reviewer, who classified no sampled holding and ran no production MRA calculation, sign the workpaper and confirm segregation.
Report the conclusion, the recomputed ratio and any Enterprise-notifiable defect to the Audit Committee and the Board Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the recomputed sufficiency ratio, a conclusion and the committee reporting dates, filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the PMIERs Section 701 capital plan stress and scenario testing — forecasting PMIERs Available Assets against Minimum Required Assets under expected and severely adverse conditions and sizing the contingent capital needed ahead of any projected shortfall

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — PMIERs (Sept 27, 2018) Section 701 Sources and Diversification of Capital, requiring a capital plan with expected and stress forecasts and contingencies to raise capital ahead of a projected shortfall; re-read alongside the 2024 Available Asset amendment because the phase-in to 9/30/2026 changes the forecast asset base

In-scope processes.value: Annual capital planning for the mortgage guaranty Approved Insurer — macroeconomic scenario selection anchored to the Federal Reserve CCAR severely adverse scenario, projection of new insurance written, delinquency and claim paths, PMIERs Available Asset and Minimum Required Asset forecasting, contingent capital sourcing and diversification, and board approval of the plan

In-scope systems.value: Stress projection engine holding the loan-level roll-forward, delinquency-to-claim transition and PMIERs asset/requirement modules; scenario inputs and results version-controlled in the model governance repository; plan pack tabled on the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: PMIERs Section 701 Capital Plan and Stress Testing Procedure — CCAR severely adverse variable mapping (HPI, unemployment, GDP, rates), loan-level projection method, delinquency and claim-rate stress calibration, PMIERs sufficiency forecast, contingent capital option inventory with lead times, and the management-action trigger ladder

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and the Chief Risk Officer and adopted by the Board Risk Committee with the annual plan; re-approved when the Federal Reserve publishes a new CCAR scenario set or the Enterprises amend PMIERs capital requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Annual cycle anchored to the Federal Reserve's CCAR scenario publication (typically February) with the run completed and the capital plan board-approved before the year's business plan is locked; sufficiency projections refreshed each quarter and any projected breach escalated to the Enterprises inside the PMIERs notification window

Deadline reminders configured.value: Capital planning calendar tasks at CCAR publication +10 business days (variables mapped), +30 days (baseline and severely adverse runs complete), +45 days (contingency options priced) and +60 days (board approval), plus a quarterly refresh task tied to the PMIERs sufficiency assessment

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Scenario variable mapping to the CCAR severely adverse file, model version and input hash, run outputs by quarter, sensitivity and reverse-stress results, contingent capital option memos, the approved capital plan and the board minute retained 7 years from the plan approval date in the compliance evidence repository

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: A missed annual run, use of a superseded CCAR scenario vintage, an unvalidated model version, or a projected PMIERs shortfall left without a costed and time-bound contingency is logged as a capital-planning exception with root cause, owner and remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Chief Actuary signs off the stress results, the assumption set and any re-run required after a validation finding, before the plan goes to the Board Risk Committee

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The full annual capital plan run — every scenario executed (baseline, severely adverse, company-specific and reverse stress), the loan-level in-force portfolio and planned new insurance written feeding it, and every contingent capital option listed in the plan

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Under the severely adverse scenario the projected PMIERs sufficiency ratio must stay at or above 100% in every projected quarter after planned management actions; a projected quarter below 100% without a costed contingency that closes it with lead time to spare is a fail, as is any scenario run on a CCAR vintage other than the current publication or on an unvalidated model version

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual, tied to the CCAR scenario publication; the test runs once per year over the full plan, with a quarterly light-touch check that the sufficiency projection has been refreshed for actual delinquency and portfolio movement

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer sits outside Actuarial and Capital Management and must not have built, calibrated or run any scenario in the plan

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual PMIERs capital plan stress-test workpaper — scenario inventory, CCAR variable trace, input reconciliation, re-performed severely adverse run, contingency feasibility assessment and exception log — in the compliance evidence repository under the plan year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Capital plan with scenario definitions and CCAR variable sources, projected Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets by quarter, sufficiency ratio paths, contingent capital inventory with lead times, model validation memo and the board approval minute, producible to an Enterprise Approved Insurer review or FHFA request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Chief Actuary answers Enterprise questions on scenario calibration and projected requirements through the Approved Insurer contacts at Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; the CFO owns any commitment on capital-raising contingencies; General Counsel clears any disclosure of a projected shortfall before it leaves the company

checklist.step: Open the annual capital plan cycle and capture the current CCAR scenario file
actions: Open a plan folder named PMIERs-701-CapitalPlan-<year> and record the scenario vintage, the projection start date and the board approval target date.
Download the Federal Reserve's published CCAR scenario set for the year — baseline and severely adverse — and save the domestic variables workbook with its publication date and file hash.

Extract the variables that drive mortgage insurance losses: house price index path, unemployment rate path, real GDP growth, 10-year Treasury and mortgage rate paths, quarter by quarter over the projection horizon.
Confirm with the Chief Risk Officer that this vintage supersedes last year's and that no scenario is being carried forward.
Record on the cycle cover sheet that the scenario is the Federal Reserve severely adverse scenario as required by the plan under PMIERs Section 701.
checklist.done: the current-year CCAR baseline and severely adverse variable paths are captured with publication date and hash in the plan folder.

checklist.step: Map the CCAR variables onto the insurance loss drivers
actions: Translate the CCAR house price index path into the model's mark-to-market LTV roll-forward at loan level, using the property valuation basis required by PMIERs Section 402.

Translate the unemployment path into the default frequency driver in the delinquency transition module, calibrated against the company's 2007-2011 experience and the last three years of actual transitions.
Set the cure rate, claim rate given delinquency and loss severity assumptions under stress and document the derivation of each with its data source.
Document any place where a CCAR variable is not used directly and state the bridging assumption and why it is defensible.
Have the Chief Actuary review and initial the assumption set before any run is executed.
checklist.done: every CCAR variable is mapped to a named model driver with a documented, Chief Actuary-initialled derivation.

checklist.step: Freeze the in-force portfolio and the planned new insurance written
actions: Take the most recent Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset as the starting in-force and confirm its RIF control total matches the version delivered to the Enterprises.
Obtain the planned new insurance written volumes, product mix, LTV and credit score distribution by quarter from the Insurance Product Manager and the business plan.
Obtain the planned ceded reinsurance and ILN structures from the Head of Reinsurance, with the PMIERs credit each is expected to attract and its Enterprise approval status.
Freeze all three inputs with a version label and record the row counts and control totals in the plan folder.
Notify the Head of Capital Management that inputs are frozen so the run can start.
checklist.done: starting in-force, planned NIW and planned ceded structures are frozen with version labels and reconciled control totals.

checklist.step: Run the expected (baseline) scenario projection
actions: Execute the baseline run over the full projection horizon at quarterly steps using the CCAR baseline variable paths.
Produce per quarter: risk-in-force, delinquency inventory, claims paid, premium earned, statutory contingency reserve build and release, Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets.
Apply the 2024 Available Asset amendment phase-in step applicable to each projected quarter through full effect on September 30, 2026, so the asset base tightens on the correct schedule.
Record the model version, input hash, run timestamp and operator in the model governance repository.
Chart the baseline sufficiency ratio path and note the minimum quarter and its value.
checklist.done: a versioned baseline run exists with a quarterly sufficiency ratio path and the phase-in applied on schedule.

checklist.step: Run the severely adverse scenario projection
actions: Execute the same model on the CCAR severely adverse variable paths, holding the frozen in-force and planned NIW constant so the scenario, not the inputs, drives the difference.

Confirm the delinquency inventory and claim payments respond to the house price and unemployment shocks and that the MRA rises as loans migrate into delinquent buckets carrying higher Exhibit B factors.
Project Available Assets under stress including investment mark-downs on the mortgage-backed holdings the amended standard already limits.
Produce the quarterly sufficiency ratio path and identify the first quarter it falls below 100% and the maximum dollar shortfall.
Record the run version, inputs and outputs in the model governance repository alongside the baseline.
checklist.done: a versioned severely adverse run exists showing the quarterly sufficiency path, the first breach quarter and the peak shortfall in dollars.

checklist.step: Add company-specific and reverse-stress scenarios
actions: Build company-specific scenarios that CCAR does not cover: loss of ceded credit when a top reinsurer is downgraded, a lender concentration failing under Sections 600-601 monitoring, and an adverse property valuation revision under Section 402.
Run a reverse stress test to find the house price decline and unemployment level at which the sufficiency ratio breaches 100% with no management action.
Express the reverse-stress result as a plain sentence — the HPI fall and unemployment rate that break the plan — for the board paper.
Compare the reverse-stress break point to the CCAR severely adverse path to show how much headroom exists beyond the regulatory scenario.
checklist.done: company-specific scenarios and a reverse-stress break point are run and stated in plain terms against the CCAR path.

checklist.step: Quantify the capital shortfall and its timing under each scenario
actions: For each scenario, tabulate the projected sufficiency ratio, the dollar cushion and the shortfall by quarter, pre and post planned management actions.
Name the first quarter any scenario breaches 100% and compute the lead time from today to that quarter in months.
Attribute the shortfall between its causes: MRA growth from delinquency migration, Available Asset reduction from the amendment phase-in, investment mark-downs, and loss of ceded credit.
State the peak capital need in dollars — the figure the contingency plan must be able to raise.
checklist.done: a scenario-by-quarter shortfall table exists with the first breach quarter, the lead time in months and an attributed peak capital need.

checklist.step: Build the contingent capital option inventory with lead times and costs
actions: Inventory each source: holding company cash downstream, undrawn revolver or contingent capital facility, surplus notes, common or preferred equity issuance, quota-share reinsurance and insurance-linked notes.

For each source record the amount available, the execution lead time in weeks, the indicative cost, the approvals required (board, state regulator, Enterprise non-objection for reinsurance credit) and any market-condition dependency.
Flag every source that is unavailable precisely when it is needed — equity issuance into a housing stress, or reinsurance capacity that reprices when losses emerge — and discount it in the plan.
Confirm the aggregate reliable capacity equals or exceeds the peak capital need with the lead time to spare, and say so explicitly if it does not.
checklist.done: each capital source has an amount, lead time, cost, approval path and stress-availability judgement, totalled against the peak need.

checklist.step: Demonstrate diversification of capital sources as Section 701 requires
actions: Show the split of contingent capacity across internal resources, debt, equity and risk transfer, and the share the single largest source represents.
Test the plan with the largest single source removed and confirm the remaining sources still cover the peak need.
Record concentration on any one counterparty, facility bank or reinsurer, and the mitigation for each.
State the conclusion on diversification in the plan text with the numbers behind it rather than as an assertion.
checklist.done: the plan shows capacity by source type, survives removal of the largest single source, and names counterparty concentrations.

checklist.step: Set the management-action trigger ladder
actions: Define trigger levels on the sufficiency ratio — for example an early-warning level, a management-action level and the PMIERs 100% floor — and set each with the board.

Attach a specific action to each level: tighten underwriting eligibility and pricing, curtail new insurance written in the highest-factor segments, accelerate the ceded reinsurance placement, draw the facility, suspend dividends to the holding company.
Name the owner and the decision forum for each action and the maximum time from trigger breach to action start.
Load the triggers into the risk platform with automated alerting off the quarterly sufficiency assessment.
checklist.done: a trigger ladder with levels, actions, owners and time limits is board-set and loaded with automated alerting.

checklist.step: Obtain independent validation of the stress model and assumptions
actions: Review the conceptual soundness of the delinquency transition and claim-rate modules and challenge the calibration against 2007-2011 and recent experience.
Re-run a benchmark cohort with an independent implementation and compare projected claims and MRA quarter by quarter.
Test sensitivity to the three assumptions that move the answer most — HPI elasticity of default, cure rate under stress, and severity — and report the range of sufficiency outcomes.
Issue a validation memo with findings graded by severity, required re-runs, and the model version and scenario vintage tested; block board tabling until high-severity findings are cleared.
checklist.done: a dated validation memo covering soundness, benchmark re-run and key sensitivities is issued and high-severity findings are cleared.

checklist.step: Write the capital plan document
actions: Draft the plan with the sections PMIERs Section 701 expects: scenario definitions and their CCAR source, projected Available Assets and Minimum Required Assets by quarter, sufficiency paths, the shortfall analysis, the diversified contingent capital inventory and the trigger ladder.
State plainly the contingency for raising additional capital ahead of any projected shortfall, with the amount, the source, the lead time and the decision date that starts it.
Attach the validation memo, the assumption documentation and the CCAR variable trace as appendices.
Circulate to the CFO, CRO and Chief Actuary for comment at least five business days before the board paper deadline.
checklist.done: a complete capital plan with scenarios, projections, contingencies and appendices is circulated for executive comment.

checklist.step: Obtain Chief Actuary sign-off on results and assumptions
actions: Review the assumption set, the severely adverse results and the validation findings together, and challenge the cure rate and severity assumptions specifically.
Confirm the scenario used is the current CCAR severely adverse vintage and that the model version is a validated one.
Sign the results certification stating the projections are a reasonable representation of the company's PMIERs position under expected and stress conditions.
Record any qualification in the certification itself with the remediation owner and date.
checklist.done: a dated Chief Actuary certification of the assumptions and results, including any qualification, is attached to the plan.

checklist.step: Take the capital plan to the Board Risk Committee for approval
actions: Publish the plan to the board portal at least five business days before the meeting with the Chief Actuary certification and validation memo attached.
Present the severely adverse sufficiency path, the first breach quarter, the peak capital need, the contingent capacity against it and the trigger ladder.
Ask the committee to resolve on the plan, the triggers and the pre-authorised contingent actions, and record the resolution, the directors present and any directed change in the minutes.
Have the Corporate Secretary file the signed minute extract with the plan folder as evidence of board approval.
checklist.done: the Board Risk Committee has approved the plan and the trigger ladder, with a signed minute extract filed.

checklist.step: Refresh the projection quarterly and archive the plan evidence
actions: Each quarter, re-run the severely adverse projection off actual in-force, actual delinquency inventory and the current phase-in step, and compare the new sufficiency path to the approved plan.
Where the first breach quarter moves closer or the peak need grows, escalate to the CRO and the Board Risk Committee before the next scheduled meeting rather than waiting for the annual cycle.

Move the plan folder — CCAR variable file, assumption documentation, all scenario runs with versions and hashes, validation memo, contingency inventory, certification and board minute — into the compliance evidence repository under PMIERs / Section 701 / <plan year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the plan approval date and confirm the record is retrievable by plan year, scenario and model version.
checklist.done: the quarterly refresh is running against the approved plan and the full plan record is archived under a 7-year retention label.

testing.step: Build the population of scenarios and runs in the annual plan
actions: Extract from the model governance repository every projection run executed for the plan year with model version, scenario name, input hash, run timestamp and operator.
Compare the run list to the scenarios described in the approved capital plan and list any scenario in the plan with no logged run, and any logged run not reflected in the plan.
Include superseded and discarded runs so scenario-shopping — re-running until the answer improves — is visible.
Sign the population as complete with the extract query and date in the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed population of all plan-year runs exists, including superseded runs, reconciled to the scenarios described in the plan.

testing.step: Trace the scenario variables back to the published CCAR severely adverse file
actions: Download the Federal Reserve's published CCAR scenario workbook for the plan year independently and check its publication date against the one in the plan folder.
Compare the house price index, unemployment, GDP and rate paths used in the run to the published severely adverse paths quarter by quarter.
Confirm the vintage used is the current publication and not a prior year's scenario carried forward.
Any variable path that differs from the published file without a documented, approved bridging assumption is an exception.
testing.done: every stress variable path is traced to the current published CCAR severely adverse file or to an approved bridging assumption.

testing.step: Reconcile the model inputs to the source of record
actions: Compare the starting in-force loan count and risk-in-force in the run to the Exhibit F Quarterly Portfolio Loan Level Dataset delivered to the Enterprises for that quarter.
Compare the planned new insurance written volumes and mix to the approved business plan tabled with the board.

Confirm the ceded structures modelled match the treaties and ILNs on the reinsurance register, and that PMIERs credit is only modelled where an Enterprise no-objection exists or is realistically expected with a stated date.
Quantify and explain any input difference above 1% of risk-in-force.
testing.done: starting in-force, planned NIW and modelled ceded structures reconcile to Exhibit F, the business plan and the reinsurance register.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of runs and loan cohorts to re-perform
actions: Take 100% of the severely adverse run and the reverse-stress run, plus the company-specific scenario with the largest modelled impact.
Take a seeded random sample of 10 loan cohorts stratified by LTV band, credit score band and vintage for detailed recomputation.
Record the seed, the strata, the cohort identifiers and the selection date so the sample can be re-drawn.
Add any assumption that carried a prior-year validation finding as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: a reproducible sample covering the severely adverse and reverse-stress runs plus stratified loan cohorts is documented.

testing.step: Re-perform the severely adverse projection on the sampled cohorts
actions: Independently roll each sampled cohort forward under the CCAR severely adverse HPI and unemployment paths using a separately coded transition and severity implementation.
Compute projected delinquency inventory, claims paid and Exhibit B-driven Minimum Required Assets by quarter for the cohort.
Compare to the production run cohort by cohort and quarter by quarter; explain any variance above 5% in projected claims or MRA down to a named assumption.
Confirm the production run applied the higher Exhibit B factors as loans migrate into delinquent buckets rather than holding performing-loan factors.
testing.done: each sampled cohort has an independent severely adverse projection agreeing within tolerance or a named assumption explaining the gap.

testing.step: Recompute the Available Asset path including the amendment phase-in
actions: Rebuild the projected Available Assets path from the starting classified holdings, applying the amendment phase-in step applicable to each projected quarter through full effect on September 30, 2026.
Apply the stress investment mark-downs to mortgage-backed and lower-credit-quality holdings and re-apply the RMBS/CRE concentration limits at each projected quarter-end.
Compare to the production Available Asset path; a path that holds today's phase-in step flat across the horizon overstates capacity and is an exception.
Recompute the sufficiency ratio path from your own Available Asset and MRA figures.
testing.done: the Available Asset and sufficiency ratio paths are independently rebuilt with the correct phase-in step in every projected quarter.

testing.step: Recompute the shortfall, the breach quarter and the lead-time maths
actions: From the recomputed sufficiency path, identify the first quarter below 100% and the peak dollar shortfall, and compare both to the plan.
Compute the lead time in months from the plan approval date to the first breach quarter.
Compare that lead time to the longest execution lead time among the capital sources the plan relies on to close the gap; a contingency that cannot execute before the breach quarter is a fail.
Confirm the peak need is measured after, not before, the planned management actions that the board actually pre-authorised.
testing.done: the breach quarter, peak shortfall and lead time are recomputed and tested against the contingency execution timeline.

testing.step: Assess whether the contingent capital sources are real and diversified
actions: For each source in the inventory, trace to primary evidence: executed facility agreement with undrawn amount and expiry, board equity authorisation, holding company liquidity statement, or a reinsurer's indicative term sheet.
Check the availability judgement under stress — an equity issuance or new reinsurance capacity assumed available in the middle of a severe housing downturn must carry a stated basis.
Re-perform the diversification test by removing the largest single source and confirming the remainder still covers the recomputed peak need.
Flag any source counted in the plan that has expired, is fully drawn, or requires an approval not yet sought.
testing.done: every contingent source is traced to primary evidence and the plan still covers the peak need with the largest source removed.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the scenario or cohort, the defect and its effect on the projected sufficiency ratio or the peak capital need.
Assign a root cause — stale CCAR vintage, flat phase-in assumption, unvalidated model version, overstated contingent capacity, ceded credit modelled without Enterprise approval — and a named owner.
Set a remediation date and, where the projected position was materially overstated, require a re-run and a re-tabling to the Board Risk Committee before the plan is relied on.
Carry every open exception into next year's test and into the next quarterly refresh as a mandatory retest item.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, a quantified effect on the sufficiency path, a root cause, an owner and a re-run decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: State whether the recomputed severely adverse sufficiency path stays at or above 100% in every quarter after board-approved actions, and whether contingencies close any gap ahead of the breach quarter.
Write the conclusion — effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective — referencing the scenario trace, cohort re-performance, Available Asset rebuild and contingency assessment.
Have the independent reviewer, who built, calibrated and ran none of the scenarios, sign the workpaper and confirm segregation in writing.
Report the conclusion and any projected shortfall to the Audit Committee and the Board Risk Committee, and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the recomputed stress conclusion, contingency adequacy and committee reporting dates, filed in the repository.
